front.title: Enforcement Profile for Agent Capabilities: Argument Constraints, Taint Propagation, and Consent Binding

abstract.t: AI agents increasingly call tools and hand work to other agents while holding broad, inherited authority. Most of the resulting incidents share one shape: an agent, often steered by injected content, performs an action its principal never authorized, and no party can prove the limit afterward. This document defines an interoperable enforcement profile that composes two existing building blocks, a delegable signed capability (the Attenuating Agent Tokens profile) and a replayable action receipt, and adds three enforcement rules that catch the common failures: argument-level constraints (including an egress host allowlist), taint propagation across a delegation chain, and a consent binding between a displayed decision and the action dispatched. Enforcement is specified at the tool-call boundary, outside the agent, so that a prompt cannot edit the limit and a verdict means the same thing across agent frameworks.
